happy.definition: feeling or showing pleasure, content, or joy.
examples: She feels happy when she spends time with friends.
We saw a huge statue in the park.

hard.definition: not easy; requiring effort; strong or solid.
examples: The rock is hard.
The crowd was hushed before the announcement.

history.definition: the study of past events; the record of what happened in the past.
examples: He likes ancient history.

hammer.definition: a heavy tool with a handle and a head used to drive nails.
examples: He used a hammer to fix the shelf.

hat.definition: a covering for the head worn for fashion or protection.
examples: She put on a hat.

hazardous.definition: dangerous or risky; likely to cause harm.
examples: Hazardous weather forced them indoors.

horror.definition: a genre of fiction or film intended to scare; a feeling of great fear.
examples: The horror scene was intense.
Factories hue fabrics in vivid tones.

hello.definition: An archaic or variant spelling; not standard in modern usage.
examples: Hello is used as a greeting.

hum.definition: A low, continuous sound, such as from bees or machinery.
examples: The steady hum of the air conditioner helped me fall asleep.
We could hear the distant hum of traffic from the highway.

hum.definition: To make a low continuous sound with the lips closed or nearly closed, or to sing without words.
examples: She hummed her favorite song while cooking dinner.
The refrigerator hums quietly in the background.

hi.definition: used to greet someone in a friendly way
examples: Hi, how are you today?
I said hi to my neighbor.
She waved and gave me a hi.

hey.definition: used to get someone’s attention or greet them casually
examples: Hey! Are you coming with us?
Hey, what’s up?

hey.definition: a casual greeting or attention call
examples: He shouted hey from across the street.

hangout.definition: a place where people usually meet to relax or socialize
examples: This café is our usual hangout.
We met at a hangout near the park.

hail.definition: small pieces of ice that fall from the sky during storms
examples: The hail damaged the car.
We stayed inside when hail started.

hail.definition: to fall as small pieces of ice
examples: It began to hail during the afternoon.
The forecast says it will hail tonight.

hour.definition: a unit of time equal to sixty minutes
examples: I will be there in an hour.
We studied for two hours.

honest.definition: truthful and not trying to steal or cheat
examples: Be honest with me.
An honest person tells the truth.

hermetic.definition: completely sealed off so that nothing can enter or leave
examples: The container was hermetic to keep out moisture.
The lab uses hermetic seals.

hermetic.definition: closed and difficult for others to understand or enter
examples: The organization can feel hermetic to outsiders.

hen.definition: a female chicken raised for eggs or meat
examples: The hen laid an egg this morning.
We saw a hen in the yard.

haggard.definition: looking tired and worn out, often due to stress or illness
examples: She looked haggard after working all night.
His haggard appearance worried me.

horizon.definition: the line where the earth and the sky seem to meet
examples: We could see mountains on the horizon.
The sun sets below the horizon.

hazy.definition: Not clear because of mist, or not easy to understand
examples: The view was hazy because of the smoke.
I have a hazy memory of that day.

hesitate.definition: To pause before doing something because you feel unsure or nervous
examples: Don’t hesitate to ask if you need help.
He hesitated before answering the question.

hush.definition: To make someone or a group become quiet
examples: The teacher hushed the class before the test.
He tried to hush the baby.

hush.definition: A quiet moment or a state of silence
examples: There was a hush in the room as the results were read.
The hush after her speech felt long.

hollow.definition: Having a space inside; not solid
examples: The statue is hollow, so it is very light.
The sound came from a hollow space under the floor.

hollow.definition: A depression or empty space in the ground
examples: They camped beside a hollow in the hills.
A hollow formed where the soil had washed away.

hollow.definition: To make something hollow by removing material
examples: The wind hollowed out the rock over years.
Workers hollowed the area for the new pipes.

hostile.definition: Angry, unfriendly, or showing strong opposition
examples: They faced hostile questions from the committee.
The neighborhood became hostile after the rumor spread.

hitherto.definition: Up to now; until this point in time
examples: I have not seen these results hitherto.
The team had not faced such problems hitherto.

hear.definition: To receive sound with your ears
examples: I can hear music from the next room.
Did you hear the announcement?

here.definition: In this place; at this location
examples: Please sit here while I check.
Is your phone here or at home?

hence.definition: For this reason; as a result of something that was just said
examples: The train was late; hence the meeting started late.
He missed the flight, hence his problem.

harmonic.definition: Related to harmony or sound waves that fit together well
examples: The harmonic overtones made the tone richer.
He used harmonic patterns in the music.

hale.definition: Healthy and strong, especially in older age
examples: He stayed hale and active even at seventy.
She is still hale after years of hard work.

haze.definition: A misty layer in the air that reduces clarity
examples: A haze covered the city in the morning.
The lights looked blurry through the haze.

haze.definition: To make the air misty or unclear
examples: Smoke hazed the sky after the fire.
The temperature change hazed the view.
H e must attend meetings henceforth.
H e agreed to call henceforth.
